frequency_question: How often do announced tariffs get successfully implemented despite structural friction without being delayed, rescinded, or replaced by a negotiated agreement?
membership_rule: Includes major unilateral tariff threats or announcements by U.S. administrations directed at major trading partners where domestic industry or statutory friction is immediately evident; excludes minor administrative antidumping duties.

cases.name: Reagan Administration Japanese Auto Import Quotas/Tariff Threats
Trump Administration Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs

provenance_note: claimed 5 hits but 4 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 5 major historical instances enumerated; historical sample shows high resolve to push through structural friction.
known_gaps: Excludes minor tariff adjustments; focuses solely on high-salience protectionist announcements.
skeleton: Total major contested tariff threats resulting in actual implementation versus those diverted by structural pushback or negotiation.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 major unilateral announcements where implementation was explicitly scheduled under high-friction conditions.
validity_reason: Executive branch trade authority under Section 232 and Section 301 remains stable across administrations.
